narration.full_text: Namaste students! Welcome to our advanced quiz on Control and Coordination. This section will challenge your understanding with some more complex questions. Let's see how well you've grasped the concepts. Pay close attention to each question. First question: How do auxins promote the growth of a tendril around a support? Describe in brief. Think about the role of auxins in cell elongation and unequal growth. Ready for the answer? Auxins produced in the shoot tip move downwards, causing cell elongation. In tendrils, auxins move away from the contact point, leading to more growth on the side away from the support, causing coiling. Moving on to the next question. Illustrate with the help of a diagram, the effect of auxins in different parts of a plant. Consider how auxin affects both shoots and roots. Here’s the answer. Auxin, formed in the apical meristem of roots and shoots, promotes cell enlargement in shoots and inhibits lateral buds, while in roots, it promotes cell division. Now, for a comparison. List in tabular form three differences in the movement of leaves of a Touch-me-not plant when touched and movement of a tendril towards a support. Think about growth dependence, speed, and direction. Let's reveal the differences. Mimosa leaves show growth-independent, fast, and non-directional movement. Tendrils show growth-dependent, slow, and directional movement. Excellent! Next question. (a) Write the names and one function of each of any three growth hormones in plants. (b) In the absence of muscle cells, how do plant cells show movement? Take a moment to recall the plant hormones and their functions, and how plants move without muscles. Here’s the detailed answer. (a) Auxin promotes cell elongation and division. Gibberellins aid stem growth. Cytokinins promote cell division and delay leaf aging. (b) Plants use electrical and chemical means to convey information for movement, like the Mimosa pudica folding leaves, which is growth-independent. Keep up the great work!

visual_beats.description: Title: Advanced Quiz: Control and Coordination
Question: How do auxins promote the growth of a tendril around a support? Describe in brief.
Thinking prompt: Auxins, cell elongation, unequal growth.

Answer: Auxins produced in the shoot tip move downwards in the plant. These auxins cause cell elongation in the growing tissues. In the tendrils, auxins move away from the point of contact with the supporting object. More growth occurs on the side away from the support. As a result of unequal growth on the two sides, the tendril coils around the support.
Question: Illustrate with the help of a diagram, the effect of auxins in different parts of a plant.

Answer: Diagram illustrating the role of auxin in plant growth. Auxin is formed in the apical meristem of the root and shoot. In the shoot, auxin promotes cell enlargement and inhibits the development of lateral buds. In the root, auxin promotes cell division.
Question: List in tabular form three differences in the movement of leaves of a Touch-me-not plant (the plant of Mimosa family) when touched and movement of a tendril towards a support.

Answer:
| S.No | Mimosa Leaves | Tendril |
|---|---|---|
| (i) | Growth independent response | Growth dependent response |
| (ii) | It is a fast process | It is a slow process |
| (iii) | It is non-directional | It is directional |

Question: (a) Write the names and one function of each of any three growth hormones in plants.
(b) In the absence of muscle cells, how do plant cells show movement?

Answer: (a) Auxin: promotes elongation and division of cell and root formation. Gibberellins: help in the growth of the stem. Cytokinins: promote cell division and delay leaf ageing.
(b) Plants use electrical and chemical means to convey information from one cell to another. For example, Mimosa pudica folds its leaves in response to touch, which is a growth-independent movement.
